s: ____ is a climate phenomenon that occurs when a vast pool of water in the eastern tropical Pacific ocean becomes abnormally warm.

El-Nino is a complex weather system that appears once every three to seven years. Consider the following state
A. The appearance of warm currents off the Coast of Peru in the Eastern Pacific.
B. The word El-Nino means ' Christ Child ' because the current appears around Christmas in December.
C. El-Nino was one of the reasons for the deficit rainfall in India (2014).
Which of the statements given above is / are correct?
x: El-Niño refers to the periodic warming of ocean waters in the eastern Pacific Ocean near the coast of Peru. The term means " Christ Child " because the phenomenon usually appears around Christmas, and it has been associated with deficit monsoon rainfall in India. including the 2014 drought.

s: Which of the following statements is not correct ?
o: El Nino is an ocean current, which appears off the
El Nino weakens the Indian Monsoon
La Nina strengthens the Indian Monsoon
x: El Nino appears as a warm oceanic current near the coast of Peru in the eastern and central tropical Pacific Ocean. El Nino generally has an adverse effect on India's Southwest Monsoon, often leading to drought like conditions. The El Nino phenomenon occurs irregularly at intervals of approximately two to seven years. La Nina is the condition opposite of an El Nino. In a La Nina the tropical Pacific trade winds become very strong and an abnormal accumulation of cold water occurs in the central and eastern Pacific Ocean.

s: Where does the El Nino current flow?
o: More than one of the above
x: EI-Nino is a complex weather system that appears once every three to seven years, bringing drought, floods and other weather extremes to different parts of the world. The system involves oceanic and atmospheric phenomena with the appearance of warm currents off the coast of Peru in the eastern Pacific and affects weather in many places including India. EI-Nino is merely an extension of the warm equatorial current which gets replaced temporarily by cold Peruvian current or Humbold current. This current increases the temperature of water on the Peruvian coast by 10°C. This results in: (i) the distortion of equatorial atmospheric circulation; (ii) irregularities in the evaporation of sea water; (iii) reduction in the amount of Planktons which further reduces the number of fish in the sea. Hence option(a) is the correct answer.

s: El-Nino develops in the
x: El-Nino is related to the eastern part of the Pacific Ocean which increases the temperature of the surface water while La Nina is related to the large pool of warm water in the western Pacific Ocean. El Nino has an adverse effect on south-west Indian monsoon whereas due to La Nina, on the western side of the Pacific Ocean, rainfall is generally heavier which activates the Indian summer monsoon as well. So both the statements are wrong.

s:
With reference to the “EL-NINO”, which of the following statement/s is/are correct?
(1) El Nino involves appearance of warm current off the coast of Peru in eastern pacific.
(2) This warm current increase the temperature of water on the Peruvian coast by 10°C there by increasing the amount of Plankton in the sea.
Select the correct answer using the code given below-
x: EI-Nino is a complex weather system that appears once every three to seven years, bringing drought, floods and other weather extremes to different parts of the world. The system involves oceanic and atmospheric phenomena with the appearance of warm currents off the coast of Peru in the eastern Pacific and affects weather in many places including India. EI-Nino is merely an extension of the warm equatorial current which gets replaced temporarily by cold Peruvian current or Humbold current. This current increases the temperature of water on the Peruvian coast by 10°C. This results in: (i) the distortion of equatorial atmospheric circulation; (ii) irregularities in the evaporation of sea water; (iii) reduction in the amount of Planktons which further reduces the number of fish in the sea. Hence option(a) is the correct answer.

s: ‘El Nino’ associated with the formation of the South-West Monsoon of India is
x: El Nino is an abnormal warm ocean current replacing the cold Peruvian current off Peru in the Pacific. It is an oceanic phenomenon, not an air mass, wind or pressure centre, though it affects the Indian monsoon.

s: During El Nino, what happens to the upwelling of cold, nutrient-rich water off the Peru coast?
x: During El Nino a warm current replaces the cold Humboldt current and upwelling stops, so phytoplankton decline and fisheries collapse.

s: The name ‘El Nino’ literally refers to which of the following?
o: The little boy or Christ child
x: El Nino means ‘the little boy’ or ‘Christ child’ and is associated with its appearance around Christmas.

s: What is El Nino?
o: A permanent warm current along the eastern coast of India
Abnormal warming of the central and eastern tropical Pacific
Abnormal cooling of the western Pacific only
A periodic reversal of the Atlantic Ocean currents
x: El Nino is the abnormal warming of the central and eastern Pacific. It is an oceanic component of the broader ENSO phenomenon.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about El Nino and La Nina?
o: El Nino is the warm phase and La Nina is the cold phase.
They can influence Indian monsoon rainfall.
They are storms that form exclusively over the eastern Pacific.
They are climate patterns associated with coupled ocean-atmosphere changes.
x: El Nino and La Nina are climate patterns, not storms; they are ocean-atmosphere phases that can affect the Indian monsoon.

s: How often does El Nino generally recur?
x: El Nino recurs irregularly, on average every 2–7 years, so 3–7 years is the closest option; it does not occur every year.

s: What happens to the easterly trade winds during the onset of El Nino?
x: In El Nino the trade winds weaken or reverse, warm western Pacific water shifts east, and the warming weakens the winds further.

s: During El Nino, rising air shifts eastward and air descends over the Indian Ocean. What does this generally produce?
o: No change in Indian monsoon conditions
High pressure and a delayed or weak Indian monsoon
Low pressure and a stronger Indian monsoon
High pressure and exceptionally heavy monsoon rainfall
x: Descending air over the Indian Ocean produces high pressure, which is associated with a delayed or weak Indian monsoon.

s: In which year was El Nino linked to a monsoon deficit of about 12% below normal in India?
x: In 2014, El Nino conditions were linked to India's monsoon deficit of about 12% below normal.

s: Which cold current off the coast of Peru is replaced by the warm El Nino current?
x: During El Nino a warm current flows south along Peru and replaces the cold Humboldt (Peruvian) current.

s: What happens to the fish catch off the coast of Peru during El Nino?
o: It shifts to cold-water species only
x: El Nino stops the cold nutrient-rich upwelling off Peru, so phytoplankton fall and the fish catch collapses.

s: Over India, El Nino has usually been the harbinger of drought. Which phenomenon instead brings rain to India?
x: La Nina La Nina, the cooling phase of the El Nino-Southern Oscillation cycle in the Pacific, is generally associated with stronger and more abundant monsoon rainfall over the Indian subcontinent.

s: Which was the seasonal factor responsible for the intense cold in northern India in January, 2012?
x: La Nina is characterized by unusually cold oceanic temperature in the Equatorial Pacific. Due to La Nina Wind, January 2012 witnessed intense cold in Northern India.

s:
La Nina is suspected to have caused recent floods in Australia. How is La Nina different from El Nino?

I. La Nina is characterised by unusually cold ocean temperature in equatorial Indian Ocean, whereas El Nino is characterised by unusually warm ocean temperature in the equatorial Pacific Ocean.

II. El Nino has adverse effect on South-West monsoon of India, but La Nina has no effect on monsoon climate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement I is wrong because La Nina cooling occurs in the central/eastern equatorial Pacific, not the Indian Ocean. Statement II is wrong because La Nina gives normal to above normal monsoon, so it does have an effect. Hence neither is correct.

s: El Nino ____ the Walker circulation and shifts it eastward.
x: El Nino weakens the Walker circulation and moves it east, reducing convection over India; La Nina strengthens it.

s: Which inference regarding El Nino and Bay of Bengal cyclones is supported by the INCOIS study?
o: El Nino may reduce post-monsoon Bay of Bengal cyclones.
El Nino always increases post-monsoon Bay of Bengal cyclones.
El Nino shifts all Bay of Bengal cyclones to the Arabian Sea.
El Nino has no relationship with Bay of Bengal cyclones.
x: The study indicated that El Nino may reduce the number of post-monsoon Bay of Bengal cyclones.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: El Nino — normal to above-normal Indian monsoon
La Nina — cooler central/eastern Pacific SST
El Nino — warmer central/eastern Pacific SST
x: El Nino is associated with a weak or below-normal Indian monsoon; normal to above-normal monsoon conditions are associated with La Nina.

s: Which of the following pairs (region – impact of La Nina) is correctly matched?
o: North India – Warmer winters and fewer cold waves
Bay of Bengal – Fewer floods and cyclones
Australia and Indonesia – Heavy rain and floods
x: La Nina brings heavy rain and floods to Australia and Indonesia, colder winters to North India and more severe cyclones in the Bay of Bengal.

s: Which year was the warmest La Nina year on record?
x: 2025 was the warmest La Nina year on record.

s: When did the last global El Nino occur?
x: The last global El Nino was in 2023-24.

x: 6 of 10 El Nino years brought depressed Indian rainfall.

s:
Consider the following statements about La Nina:

2. It brings heavy rain and floods to Australia and Indonesia.

x: La Nina has stronger trades and brings floods to Australia and Indonesia, but it strengthens the Walker circulation; El Nino weakens it.

x: El Nino shifts rising air east, so Australia and Indonesia turn drier; La Nina brings them heavy rain and floods.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about types of El Nino?
o: 'Modoki' is a Japanese word meaning 'returning child'.
In a canonical El Nino, maximum warming occurs in the eastern Pacific near Peru.
In El Nino Modoki, maximum warming occurs in the central Pacific.

s: Where does maximum warming occur in a canonical (normal) El Nino?
x: Canonical El Nino peaks in the eastern Pacific near Peru; Modoki peaks in the central Pacific.

s: 'Modoki', meaning 'similar but different', is a word from which language?

s: In the normal Walker circulation over the tropical Pacific, where does air rise?
x: Normally air rises over the warm western Pacific and Indonesia, sinks over the cool eastern Pacific, with easterly trades at the surface.

s: In the normal Walker circulation, where does air sink?
x: Normally air rises over the warm western Pacific and Indonesia, flows east aloft and sinks over the cool eastern Pacific.

s: Which surface winds complete the normal Walker loop by returning westward?
x: In the normal Walker loop, surface easterly trades return the air westward.

s:
With reference to the planet Earth, consider the following statements:
1. Rain forests produce more oxygen than that produced by oceans. Environment and Ecology PMF IAS E&E – 37
2. Marine phytoplankton and photosynthetic bacteria produce about 50% of world's oxygen.
3. Well-oxygenated surface water contains several folds higher oxygen than that in atmospheric air.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
o: None of the above statements is correct
x: Statement 1 is incorrect: The amount of oxygen produced in the Ocean is much greater (50-70%) than the oxygen produced by rainforests on land (estimated at 30%). Statement 2 is correct: Approximately half of all the oxygen on Earth comes from phytoplankton in the ocean. Larger kelp and seaweed are also producers of oxygen in the ocean. This brings the total ocean oxygen production up to 50-80%. The smallest photosynthetic organism, Prochlorococcus, produces 20% of the world's oxygen all alone. Statement 3 is incorrect: This is scientifically inaccurate. Even well-oxygenated water holds far less oxygen than air. Dissolved oxygen in water is typically 8 – 14 mg/L, whereas atmospheric air contains ~210,000 mg/L of oxygen (21% of 1,000,000 mg/L). PMF Concept Hack: Using a basic understanding, Statement 1 can be eliminated because most of the oxygen comes from the oceans (phytoplankton), not rainforests. Statement 3 is also incorrect, as it exaggerates—water does not contain several times as much oxygen as air. Statement 2 is a known fact that marine phytoplankton and photosynthetic bacteria produce about half of the world's oxygen. Hence, only Statement 2 is correct → (b).

s: In the marine environment, the main primary producers are

s:
What would happen if phytoplankton of an ocean is completely destroyed for some reason?

I. The ocean as a carbon sink would be adversely affected.

II. The food chains in the ocean would be adversely affected.

III. The density of ocean water would drastically decrease.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Phytoplankton are the base of ocean food chains and take up CO2 through photosynthesis, so losing them harms the food chains and the carbon sink (I and II). Water density depends on temperature and salinity, not on phytoplankton, so III is wrong.

s: Approximately how much of Earth’s oxygen is produced by the oceans, mainly through phytoplankton?
x: The oceans, mainly through phytoplankton, produce about half or more than half of Earth’s oxygen, exceeding the contribution of all rainforests combined.

s: What are ocean organisms that swim actively called?
x: Nekton swim actively, benthos live on the bottom, and plankton (phyto- and zoo-) drift.

s: Which are the main primary producers of the ocean?
x: Phytoplankton such as diatoms, dinoflagellates and cyanobacteria are the ocean's main primary producers.

s: What are marine organisms that live on the sea bottom called?
x: Benthos live on the bottom; nekton swim actively and plankton drift with the water.

s:

Increases nutrient supply to coastal waters
Cools the sea surface off Peru

s: Upwelling off Somalia during the south-west monsoon is linked to which current?
x: Somalia's upwelling is tied to the Findlater current in the SW monsoon; Benguela is off Namibia and Humboldt off Peru-Chile.

s: Upwelling off Peru and Chile supports a rich fishery of:
x: The Humboldt upwelling off Peru-Chile supports anchoveta; Kerala's monsoon upwelling supports oil sardine and mackerel.
